content.title: About
content.content: Breakfast pastry (NFS) is a ready‑to‑eat product that comes as a layered or yeasted bakery item designed for a quick morning meal. It typically contains flour, eggs, milk, sugar, and a modest amount of fat, and is often fortified with vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The product is made for convenience: a 2–3 minute heat in a microwave or oven is enough.
Whole‑grain flour is frequently used, increasing the fiber content.
NFS stands for "Nutrition For Start," indicating a balanced macro‑nutrient profile.
Available in sweet (with berries, chocolate) and savory (with cheese, ham) versions.
Commonly used in schools and offices as a fast breakfast option.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates provide quick energy to start the day.

items.title: Protein rich
items.content: Eggs and dairy ingredients supply a notable amount of protein for muscle maintenance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fortified with B1, B2, B6 and folate, which support carbohydrate metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Dairy components help strengthen bones and teeth.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain versions contain dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Contains wheat, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Dairy and egg allergy
items.content: Includes milk and eggs, which can trigger reactions in allergic individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet varieties may have high sugar levels; diabetics should monitor portion size.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Savory versions can be high in salt, which is not recommended for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the pastry in a microwave (30‑60 seconds) or oven (180 °C, 5‑7 minutes). Top with fresh fruit, berries, honey, nuts, or low‑fat cottage cheese for added flavor and nutrition.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the original packaging in a cool, dry place. After opening, consume within 3‑5 days or transfer to the refrigerator, where it lasts up to 10 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.
